# Overview

Omix was originally built around human and mouse transcriptomics/proteomics,
via `organism = "human"` (backed by `EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86`) and
`organism = "mouse"` (backed by `org.Mm.eg.db`) in `generate_multiassay()`.
Neither Ensembl-gene-ID conventions, gene-biotype annotation, nor these two
species are universal, so bacterial/archaeal data needs a different
annotation path into the same pipeline.

`generate_multiassay()`'s `organism` argument now resolves in one of three
ways:

1. `"human"` / `"mouse"` -- unchanged, built-in annotation.
2. **Any other string naming an installed Bioconductor annotation package**
   following the `org.*.eg.db` convention (e.g. `"org.EcK12.eg.db"` for
   *E. coli* K-12, or `"org.Sco.eg.db"` for *Streptomyces coelicolor*).
   Such a package can be built for *any* organism with no existing
   package -- including essentially all non-model bacteria/archaea -- via
   [`AnnotationForge::makeOrgPackage()`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/AnnotationForge/inst/doc/MakingNewOrganismPackages.html)
   from a Prokka/Bakta/eggNOG-mapper annotation.
3. If neither of the above resolves, a user-supplied **`annotation`
   data.frame** (rownames matching the raw RNA/protein IDs, with `gene_name`
   and optionally `gene_biotype` columns) is used instead -- the practical
   default for a freshly-annotated draft genome with no Bioconductor
   package at all.

If none of the three resolve, Omix does **not** error: it emits a warning
and continues with the raw IDs as gene names and no biotype annotation
(so, e.g., `process_rna(..., protein_coding = TRUE)` becomes a no-op with
its own warning, rather than silently dropping every gene).

This vignette walks through both non-eukaryote paths on a small synthetic
bacterial dataset, and notes which downstream Omix features remain
eukaryote/mammalian-specific and should be skipped.

```{r results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(Omix)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
```

# Synthetic bacterial dataset

We simulate a tiny RNA + protein dataset for a hypothetical bacterium,
with locus-tag-style feature IDs (e.g. `STM0001`, as used by *Salmonella*
Typhimurium and similarly by many other RefSeq/Prokka/Bakta bacterial
annotations).

```{r}
set.seed(1)
n_genes <- 20
n_samples <- 6
locus_tags <- paste0("STM", sprintf("%04d", seq_len(n_genes)))

rawdata_rna <- as.data.frame(
  matrix(rnbinom(n_genes * n_samples, mu = 200, size = 5),
         nrow = n_genes, dimnames = list(locus_tags, paste0("s", seq_len(n_samples))))
)
rawdata_protein <- as.data.frame(
  matrix(rpois(n_genes * n_samples, lambda = 500),
         nrow = n_genes, dimnames = list(locus_tags, paste0("s", seq_len(n_samples))))
)

individual_metadata <- data.frame(
  id = colnames(rawdata_rna),
  diagnosis = rep(c("control", "treated"), length.out = n_samples),
  condition = rep(c(0, 1, 1, 0), length.out = n_samples) # a covariate, independent of `diagnosis`
)
metadata_rna <- individual_metadata[, -1, drop = FALSE]
rownames(metadata_rna) <- individual_metadata$id
metadata_protein <- metadata_rna

map_rna <- data.frame(primary = colnames(rawdata_rna), colname = colnames(rawdata_rna))
map_protein <- data.frame(primary = colnames(rawdata_protein), colname = colnames(rawdata_protein))
```

# Path A -- a real installed `org.*.eg.db` package

If a Bioconductor annotation package exists for your organism, pass its
package name directly as `organism`. It's resolved dynamically via
`requireNamespace()`, so this works the same way for any package
following the `org.*.eg.db` convention -- including ones built with
`AnnotationForge::makeOrgPackage()`.

This chunk only runs if `org.EcK12.eg.db` happens to be installed (it
isn't one of Omix's own dependencies, so the base install doesn't carry
it) -- it's here to show what the fully-automatic path looks like when a
package is available, without forcing every Omix install to carry an
annotation package for every possible demo organism.

```{r eval=requireNamespace("org.EcK12.eg.db", quietly = TRUE)}
multiassay_pkg <- generate_multiassay(
  rawdata_rna = rawdata_rna,
  rawdata_protein = rawdata_protein,
  individual_to_sample = FALSE,
  map_rna = map_rna,
  map_protein = map_protein,
  metadata_rna = metadata_rna,
  metadata_protein = metadata_protein,
  individual_metadata = individual_metadata,
  map_by_column = "id",
  rna_qc_data = FALSE,
  rna_qc_data_matrix = NULL,
  organism = "org.EcK12.eg.db"
)

head(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(multiassay_pkg[["rna_raw"]]))
```

# Path B -- no package available: a user-supplied annotation table

Most non-model bacteria/archaea have no Bioconductor annotation package.
The practical path there is a small annotation table -- for example
exported from Prokka/Bakta (`.tsv`) or eggNOG-mapper output -- with
rownames matching the raw IDs and `gene_name`/`gene_biotype` columns.

```{r}
annotation_table <- data.frame(
  gene_name = paste0("gene", seq_len(n_genes)),
  gene_biotype = rep(c("protein_coding", "ncRNA"), c(16, 4)),
  row.names = locus_tags
)
head(annotation_table)

multiassay <- generate_multiassay(
  rawdata_rna = rawdata_rna,
  rawdata_protein = rawdata_protein,
  individual_to_sample = FALSE,
  map_rna = map_rna,
  map_protein = map_protein,
  metadata_rna = metadata_rna,
  metadata_protein = metadata_protein,
  individual_metadata = individual_metadata,
  map_by_column = "id",
  rna_qc_data = FALSE,
  rna_qc_data_matrix = NULL,
  organism = "salmonella_typhimurium", # not an installed package -> falls back to `annotation`
  annotation = annotation_table
)

SummarizedExperiment::rowData(multiassay[["rna_raw"]])
```

## What happens with no annotation source at all

If `organism` doesn't resolve and no `annotation` table is supplied
either, Omix warns and continues rather than erroring -- gene names fall
back to the raw IDs, and biotype is left unset:

```{r}
multiassay_bare <- generate_multiassay(
  rawdata_rna = rawdata_rna,
  rawdata_protein = rawdata_protein,
  individual_to_sample = FALSE,
  map_rna = map_rna,
  map_protein = map_protein,
  metadata_rna = metadata_rna,
  metadata_protein = metadata_protein,
  individual_metadata = individual_metadata,
  map_by_column = "id",
  rna_qc_data = FALSE,
  rna_qc_data_matrix = NULL,
  organism = "salmonella_typhimurium"
)
```

# Processing transcriptomics data

`process_rna()`'s `protein_coding` filter needs `gene_biotype` annotation.
With Path B's annotation table (which included `gene_biotype`), it works
as normal:

```{r}
multiassay <- process_rna(
  multiassay = multiassay,
  transformation = "log2",
  protein_coding = TRUE,
  min_count = 1,
  min_sample = 0.1,
  dependent = "diagnosis",
  levels = c("control", "treated"),
  covariates = "condition",
  filter = TRUE,
  batch_correction = FALSE,
  batch = NULL,
  remove_sample_outliers = FALSE
)
```

Without any resolved `gene_biotype` (the "no annotation source" case
above), leave `protein_coding = FALSE` -- otherwise `process_rna()` skips
the filter itself, with a warning, rather than dropping every gene:

```{r}
multiassay_bare <- process_rna(
  multiassay = multiassay_bare,
  transformation = "log2",
  protein_coding = FALSE,
  min_count = 1,
  min_sample = 0.1,
  dependent = "diagnosis",
  levels = c("control", "treated"),
  covariates = "condition",
  filter = TRUE,
  batch_correction = FALSE,
  batch = NULL,
  remove_sample_outliers = FALSE
)
```

# Downstream analysis: what carries over unchanged, and what doesn't

The rest of the pipeline splits into three groups:

## Organism-agnostic (no changes needed)

Differential expression, WGCNA, sPLS, MOFA2/MEFISTO, DIABLO/sMB-PLS,
iCluster, network analysis and reporting all operate on the processed
numeric matrices and don't depend on organism at all:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
multiassay <- rna_DE_analysis(
  multiassay = multiassay,
  dependent = "diagnosis",
  levels = c("control", "treated"),
  filter_protein_coding = TRUE,
  log2FoldChange = 0.2
)

multiassay <- vertical_integration(
  multiassay,
  slots = c("rna_processed", "protein_processed"),
  integration = "DIABLO",
  intersect_genes = FALSE,
  ID_type = "gene_name",
  dependent = "diagnosis",
  levels = c("control", "treated"),
  design = "cor",
  ncomp = 2,
  range = list(mRNA = seq(5, 20, by = 5), proteins = seq(5, 20, by = 5))
)
```

## Organism-agnostic, but need a non-human gene set / GMT

`GSEA()` (`R/fgsea.R`) and `Transcription_Factor_enrichment()`
(`R/TF_enrichment.R`) already accept a user-supplied GMT file -- neither
calls a human-specific database internally. For bacteria, source gene
sets from:

- **Pathway enrichment** (`GSEA(geneset = ...)`): KEGG bacterial pathway
  GMTs, COG functional categories, or an eggNOG-mapper GMT export.
- **TF/regulon enrichment** (`Transcription_Factor_enrichment(TF_gmt = ...)`):
  a regulon GMT from [RegulonDB](https://regulondb.ccg.unam.mx/) (*E.
  coli*) or [CollecTF](https://www.collectf.org/) rather than the default
  Enrichr/CHEA3 (human/mouse) file.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
bacterial_gmt <- "path/to/kegg_or_cog_pathways.gmt"
gsea_result <- GSEA(gene_list = ranked_genes, pval = 0.05, geneset = bacterial_gmt)
```

## Eukaryote/mammalian-specific -- skip these for prokaryotic data

A few Omix features have no bacterial equivalent and should simply not be
used on prokaryotic data:

- **`EWCE` cell-type enrichment** (`enrichment.R`) -- needs a single-cell
  reference (`ctd`) of the kind that exists for mammalian tissues, not
  bacteria.
- **`open_targets.R`** -- queries the OpenTargets human disease-target
  platform; there's no bacterial equivalent.
- **`integrated_enrichment_multiGSEA.R`** -- `multiGSEA`'s pathway
  databases are themselves restricted to a small set of eukaryotic
  species.
- **`get_module_annotation()`** (WGCNA module GO annotation, `get.R`) --
  its underlying `WGCNA::GOenrichmentAnalysis()` only supports a fixed
  organism list (human/mouse/rat/fly/worm); for any other `organism` it
  now warns and returns `NULL` rather than erroring.
- **Pseudotime/trajectory inference** (`pseudotime_inference.R`) -- a
  single-cell eukaryotic concept; not meaningful for bulk bacterial data.

None of these are called automatically by `process_rna()`,
`vertical_integration()`, or the report generators above -- they're
opt-in functions you simply don't call for a prokaryotic project.
